Chapter 1: Childhood in a World of Unquestioned Rules
There’s something comforting about predictability, isn’t there? Especially for a child. In a small, close-knit community tucked away from everything else, life falls into a rhythm—a rhythm set by shared beliefs and unspoken routines.
Imagine growing up in the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, or FLDS. Every day, from sunrise to sunset, is shaped by rules that feel as old as the desert hills outside your window. The air almost hums with the sense that everything—what you wear, how you speak, even whom you trust—has already been decided for you.
Inside one of these homes, a young girl quickly learns that obedience is the highest virtue. Her world is a swirl of siblings, the steady buzz of daily chores, and the ever-present watchful eyes of parents who truly believe they’re protecting their children’s souls. The father is more than just a provider—he’s the family’s spiritual anchor. And the mother, gentle but equally bound by tradition, teaches her daughters to be modest, to serve, and above all, to never question the men who lead them.
Most days, laughter is there, but it’s muffled by the weight of expectation. Curiosity about the world beyond those borders? Well, there’s almost no room for that. Stories about outsiders always come with a warning: if you leave, you’re lost; if you stay, you’re chosen. The girls spend their time braiding each other’s hair and whispering about the future, but even their dreams are shaped by the teachings that surround them. Marriage, motherhood, and unwavering faith—that’s the path they see.
But here’s where it gets interesting—sometimes, just beneath the surface, small cracks start to appear. Maybe a child wonders why some rules feel so strict, or why a parent’s affection can turn into stern silence without warning. Every once in a while, the outside world sneaks in—a glimpse of a stranger, or a forbidden flash on a smuggled television. These moments are quickly brushed aside, but even so, they plant seeds of doubt.
At the very top of this world stands the community’s leader—a man seen as a prophet. His word isn’t just respected—it’s law. Questioning him? That’s simply unthinkable. From a young age, children learn that their worth is tied to how pure and obedient they are. For girls, especially, the message is clear: their bodies and their futures aren’t theirs to claim. They belong to the faith, to their fathers, and later on, to the husbands chosen for them.
As time passes, the young girl’s world seems to shrink. Friendships are carefully watched, education is limited, and even the smallest hint of rebellion is corrected right away. Still, every once in a while, there’s a moment of quiet resistance—a longing look at a forbidden book, or a hushed conversation about what life might be like somewhere else. These acts are hidden quickly, but they linger in her heart.
Most people outside this community just can’t imagine the strength of loyalty—and the fear—that binds these families together. Walking away isn’t just about leaving home; it means losing everything. Family, friends, faith, and the only identity you’ve ever known. For a child in this world, the idea of escape feels as far away as the stars.
But here’s the thing—even in the most tightly controlled places, the human spirit finds ways to question, to hope, and to dream of something more. Once those seeds of doubt are planted, they’re almost impossible to pull out. Over time, they grow into quiet questions—questions that, no matter how hard anyone tries, just won’t be silenced.
